boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along corridors immediately around Spelman and the Atlanta University Center, each with one verified reason to stop.

cards.title: Use the study rooms
cards.subtitle: Peeples Street SW corridor
cards.notes: Bring a library card or plan a walk-in visit, then ask staff about reserving a study room or using the computer lab.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop with study rooms, meeting rooms, and a computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: West End Library at 525 Peeples Street SW lists a computer lab, meeting rooms, and study rooms.
cards.source_title: West End Branch | Fulton County Library System
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and room policies before going.

cards.title: See African-diaspora art
cards.subtitle: Peeples Street SW corridor
cards.notes: Plan for the weekend hours, then spend time with the galleries in this historic West End house rather than rushing through.
cards.short_summary: A 503 Peeples Street museum with galleries and rotating art experiences.
cards.evidence_claim: Hammonds House Museum lists its location at 503 Peeples Street SW and presents gallery experiences for visitors.
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; admission is charged.

cards.title: Study the Beaux-Arts house
cards.subtitle: University Place SW corridor
cards.notes: Check tour arrangements before heading over, then look for the exterior details and read the site history of the house museum.
cards.short_summary: A landmark house museum and archives on University Place beside the AUC.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Atlanta identifies the Herndon Home at 587 University Place SW as a landmark and says the foundation operates it as an archives and house museum.
cards.access_notes: Confirm visitor and tour availability with the museum before a visit.

cards.title: Browse the collection
cards.subtitle: James P. Brawley Drive SW corridor
cards.notes: Enter through the CAU campus as directed, and allow time for the museum’s collection and current exhibition programming.
cards.short_summary: A free university art museum documenting African Americans’ role in U.S. history and culture.
cards.evidence_claim: CAUAM says it collects, preserves, researches, and exhibits art documenting African Americans in American history and culture; its FAQ states admission is free with a suggested donation.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m., and by appointment; campus access directions are posted by CAU.

cards.title: Make it a transit link
cards.subtitle: Lee Street SW corridor
cards.notes: Use the station as the handoff point for rail or bus travel, and check service alerts before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A MARTA station with rail and bus connections on the Lee Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: MARTA lists West End Station among its train stations and notes 472 parking spaces and bathrooms at the location.
cards.access_notes: Consult MARTA’s live schedules and service alerts; fares may apply.

cards.title: Find a Black-author read
cards.subtitle: Lee Street SW corridor
cards.notes: Browse fiction, nonfiction, children’s books, and history titles, or check the shop’s event listing before you walk over.
cards.short_summary: An independent bookstore at 451 Lee Street SW focused on books and literary events.
cards.evidence_claim: 44th & 3rd Bookseller lists its shop at 451 Lee Street SW, while Discover Atlanta describes its selection of Black authors and stories.
cards.access_notes: The shop lists Tuesday–Saturday and Sunday hours; purchasing a book is optional.

cards.title: Follow the trail-side reuse
cards.subtitle: Lee Street SW and White Street SW corridor
cards.notes: Walk the former warehouse corridor and use the posted tenant information to choose a daytime food, retail, or community stop.
cards.short_summary: A 23-acre mixed-use destination directly along the Westside Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Lee + White describes itself as a 23-acre, 11-building creative mixed-use destination directly along the Westside Trail.
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses set their own hours, prices, and age policies.

cards.title: Take a multi-use loop
cards.subtitle: Westside Trail corridor
cards.notes: Start at a marked access point and choose a short out-and-back walk, roll, or bike ride while following trail etiquette.
cards.short_summary: A 3.2-mile trail through historic westside neighborhoods with art displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlanta BeltLine says the Westside Trail extends 3.2 miles from I-20 to W. Marietta Street and is suited to walking, scooters, bikes, and skates.
cards.access_notes: Use designated trail entrances and follow posted trail etiquette.

cards.title: Visit the story house
cards.subtitle: Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard SW corridor
cards.notes: Reserve or confirm a visit before you go, then pair the historic house with its writing and storytelling programming.
cards.short_summary: The historic home of Joel Chandler Harris at 1050 Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard SW.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wren’s Nest identifies itself as the home of Joel Chandler Harris at 1050 Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard SW.
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are listed as 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; Sunday–Friday visits are by appointment.

cards.title: Read the historic landscape
cards.subtitle: Westview Drive SW corridor
cards.notes: Stay on walks and roadways, move quietly, and call ahead if you want to see the Abbey or another specific area.
cards.short_summary: A historic Atlanta cemetery with a gatehouse, mausoleum, and documented visitor rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Westview Cemetery says it was established in 1884, is listed in the National and Georgia Registers of Historic Places, and includes the Westview Abbey.
cards.access_notes: This is an active private cemetery; follow its visitor rules and current gate hours.
